$comment: AFLDB-ISSUE-118 Stage D1 — direct AFL Tables acquisitions that fitzRoy 1.8.0 cannot supply. The accepted fitzRoy core baseline (tools/rebuild/fitzroy/fitzroy-contract.json) remains the canonical AFL Tables source for matches, player-match rows, identities and the player_details register; this contract adds bounded, manifest-pinned page families read from afltables.com itself, each justified by a column fitzRoy drops. Nothing here adjudicates: every artefact is raw evidence a loader reconciles fail-closed through the identities the fitzRoy stage registered.

http_policy.user_agent_rule: The same User-Agent the pinned fitzRoy 1.8.0 presents to afltables.com (fitzRoy:::fitzroy_user_agent()), so this acquisition is indistinguishable in load and courtesy from the accepted baseline's own register capture.
http_policy.robots_txt: fetched once per run and recorded (status + sha256 when present); afltables.com returned 404 on 2026-09-05, i.e. no exclusion policy is published
http_policy.terminal_failure_rule: any club page that is not HTTP 200 after the retry policy is TERMINAL: the club is never written as empty and the manifest is not written at all

club_player_lists.$comment: One page per club: https://afltables.com/afl/stats/alltime/<slug>.html, the all-time player list with Cap, #, Player (linked to the profile page), DOB, HT, WT, Games (W-D-L), Goals, Seasons, Debut, Last. These are the very pages fitzRoy::fetch_player_details_afltables() reads for the register, but fitzRoy 1.8.0 drops the DOB column and the profile hrefs (select(-'DOB'); html_table() keeps no links), so the accepted register cannot supply dates of birth and cannot be joined by URL. This family keeps both. The 21 club slugs and labels are fitzRoy 1.8.0's own mapping (get_player_details_afltables), so the population is the same 21 pages the register came from.
club_player_lists.scope_rule: Every listed club, every run. There is no partial-club mode: a subset could not describe the population, and the loader's coverage gates assume all 21 pages.
club_player_lists.header_rule: The first table's header row must equal required_header exactly (order included). A changed page layout is a terminal failure, never a best-effort parse.
club_player_lists.row_rule: A data row is a row whose Player cell carries an href; the trailing totals row has none and is not data. Every kept row must carry an href: a player row without a link is a terminal failure.
club_player_lists.artefact_rule: One CSV per club under parsed/, values kept as the page prints them (no numeric coercion, blank stays blank); the raw HTML bytes kept under raw/ with their sha256. The manifest binds both.
club_player_lists.identity_rule: profile_path is the profile href reduced exactly as tools/migration/import_fitzroy_core.py normalise_profile_url() reduces it ('../' removed, the https://afltables.com/afl/stats/ prefix stripped, no leading slash) and is the ONLY key a loader may join on. A rendered name is never identity. A profile_path that resolves to no canonical identity is reported and refused, never matched by name.
club_player_lists.duplicate_rule: A profile_path may appear once per club page (a player has one row per club); the same profile_path across two club pages is the same person and must carry the same DOB — a disagreement is a loader finding, never silently resolved.

accepted_snapshot.evidence: 21 pages, 16,731 rows (the register's exact row count), 13,364 distinct profile paths, 0 cross-club date disagreements; on the rebuilt afldb_test 13,260 paths resolve to canonical identities, 104 do not (92 are 2026 debutants the 2025-terminal baseline lacks, 12 are profiles renumbered after 2026-09-02), 12,400 NULL dates fillable, 853 existing dates agree, 2 disagree (kept)

measured.$comment: What the rebuild's `birth-dates` stage must reproduce on the accepted fitzRoy baseline + this snapshot; the final validation gates read these (tools/db/rebuild-test.ts birthDateChecks) and never type them. players_with_dob = 855 fitzRoy per-match dates + 12,400 filled here; dob_without_evidence must be 0 (every date carries dob_evidence_id); players_with_club_list_birth_evidence = every canonical player a page row reached (13,255 = 13,260 resolved paths less the 5 blank cells); club_list_birth_conflict_players = players reached with two different page dates (never filled; 0 in this capture); dob_disagreeing_with_club_list = players whose retained fitzRoy date differs from the page's (Roan Steele afldb 11043, Jack Hayes afldb 6330 — recorded, adjudication is a separate decision).

club_player_lists.accepted_snapshot_rule: Set to {label, manifest, manifest_sha256_lf} by the session that accepts a capture for the rebuild's birth-date stage; the rebuild refuses a missing or mismatched pin, exactly like afl-api-contract.json roster.accepted_snapshot.

coaches.$comment: AFLDB-ISSUE-118 Stage E2 (runbook §23.27). The accepted fitzRoy baseline's per-match Coach column names one coach per (match, club) but does not KEY the person: 16 of its 383 strings name two or three canonical players (Ron Barassi, Mark Williams …) and 18 name nobody who ever played. The AFL Tables coaches index (one page per person who coached, 386 on 2026-09-05, every name distinct) keys the person, and each coach page's 'Player Stats' link is the exact players/<L>/<Name>.html profile path external_identities already holds, so a coach who played joins the existing player row through AFLDB's own identity key and a coach who never played (no link) is a coach-only person with no player row. This family captures the index and every coach page; the loader (tools/migration/import_match_coaches.py) reconciles the snapshot column to these pages by EXACT string and refuses anything else.
coaches.scope_rule: The whole index, every run: every coach row of the index's first table and every page it links. There is no partial mode; the loader refuses a manifest whose page count differs from its index row count.
coaches.index_header_rule: The index's first table's second header row must equal index_required_header exactly (the first header row is the Home & Away / Finals / Total group row). A changed layout is a terminal failure.
coaches.index_row_rule: A data row is a row whose Coach cell carries an href to a page in the coaches directory; every data row must carry one. The rendered name is kept verbatim as name_raw ('Surname, Given' — the exact form the fitzRoy Coach column prints) and must be unique across the index.
coaches.page_rule: Each coach page must carry an <h1> (display_name), and its 'Player Stats' link, when present, is reduced to a profile_path exactly as club_player_lists.identity_rule reduces one. 'Born:' is kept as printed (blank when absent). games_coached is the number of rows of the page's 'Games Coached' table — the source's own count, kept only as cross-check evidence against the snapshot column and never as a total.
coaches.artefact_rule: parsed/coaches_index.csv (one row per index row, index_columns) and parsed/coach_pages.csv (one row per page, page_columns), LF line endings, values as the page prints them; these two parsed artefacts are TRACKED (the rebuild's input bytes) and the raw HTML under raw/ is gitignored but hash-bound in the manifest. The loader always verifies the parsed artefacts against the tracked manifest and verifies the raw bytes whenever raw/ is present.
coaches.identity_rule: coach_path (coaches/<file>) is the coach's identity and profile_path the ONLY key a loader may use to link a coach to a player. A snapshot Coach string that is not exactly one index name_raw is refused; a profile_path that resolves to no canonical afltables identity is refused, never matched by name; a page with no Player Stats link is a coach-only person (player_id NULL, link_status unmatched).

profile_link_corrections.$comment: A coach page's Player Stats href that AFL Tables itself does not serve. Each rule names ONE coach page and the exact href its page prints, and supplies the profile path that IS served and that the fitzRoy url column (external_identities) holds. Applied by exact (coach_path, page_profile_path) match, never by name; every rule must match exactly one page of the accepted snapshot or the loader refuses, so a fixed page cannot leave a rule silently applying to nothing. Evidence is recorded per rule.

accepted_snapshot.evidence: 386 index rows, 386 pages (extraction 2026-09-05T06:36:13Z), 386 distinct names; 368 pages link a Player Stats profile, 18 do not (the coach-only people: Worrall, Fagan, Craig, Cahill, Bolton, Kinnear, McCartney, Brittain, Todd …); every one of the accepted baseline's 383 Coach strings and the supplement's 2 resolve to an index name by exact string; 4 page hrefs AFL Tables does not serve as printed are corrected by the tracked profile_link_corrections on dated evidence; on the rebuilt afldb_test the 32,452 (match, club) groups with a coach fold to 32,034 assignments on the 16,838 baseline matches (418 groups are 2026 supplement rows of a season the baseline does not hold), 364 of 386 coach pages' own Games Coached equal the canonical assignment count (the rest are the source's pre-1923/1940 gaps and 2026).

measured.$comment: What the rebuild's `coaches` stage must reproduce on the accepted fitzRoy baseline + pinned supplement + this snapshot; the final validation gates read these (tools/db/rebuild-test.ts coachChecks) and never type them. coaches = every index page (a person exists whether or not the column names them yet); coaches_linked_to_players = pages whose Player Stats profile resolves through external_identities (link_status unique), coaches_unlinked = pages with no profile link (player_id NULL, no players row ever created); match_coaches = (match, club) assignments on canonical matches; the three match counts are the source's own coverage shape (both coaches / one / neither — gaps only before 1923 plus eleven 1940 records) and sum to the 16,838 baseline matches.

coaches.accepted_snapshot_rule: Set to {label, manifest, manifest_sha256_lf, accepted_on, accepted_in, evidence, measured} by the session that accepts a capture for the rebuild's coaches stage; the rebuild refuses a missing or mismatched pin, exactly like club_player_lists.accepted_snapshot.
